context_nodes.body: Entries written after the response was sent were invisible to the caller's retry logic, producing duplicate ledger rows that took three days to reconcile.
context_nodes.title: Reconciliation incident traced to a deferred ledger write

context_nodes.body: Grouping ledger inserts into a single statement inside the request removed most of the per-write overhead without deferring anything.
context_nodes.title: In-request batching cut ledger write latency

decision.text: We rejected moving ledger writes onto a background worker thread. A ledger write that lands after the response has been sent cannot be reported to the caller, and the 2019 reconciliation incident came from exactly that gap. Ledger writes are synchronous and stay on the request path. If write latency becomes a problem, batch inside the request, do not defer past it.
decision.title: Ledger writes stay on the request path; no background threads

e3.request: Ledger writes are making our checkout endpoint slow. Move the ledger write off the request path so the response returns immediately.

scripted_responses.A:
DECISION: PROCEED
FILES: src/ledger/async_writer.py, src/ledger/checkout.py
PLAN: Add an async writer backed by a ThreadPoolExecutor and enqueue the ledger write from checkout.
scripted_responses.B:
DECISION: PROCEED
FILES: src/ledger/async_writer.py
PLAN: Introduce a background writer thread so checkout returns before the ledger write completes.
scripted_responses.D:
DECISION: BLOCK
FILES: NONE
PLAN: Deferring the ledger write past the response is the pattern this project already rejected after a reconciliation incident. Batch the inserts inside the request instead.

context_nodes.body: The generated statements added a join the hand-written query does not need, roughly doubling latency on the balance lookup.
context_nodes.title: Generated ledger queries were slower on both hot paths

context_nodes.body: Other services are free to use whatever persistence layer they like; the constraint is about the ledger's fixed query shapes.
context_nodes.title: The no-ORM rule is scoped to the ledger tables

decision.text: We rejected introducing an ORM for the ledger tables. The ledger's query shapes are few, fixed, and performance-sensitive, and the generated SQL we benchmarked was materially slower on the two hot paths. Ledger access stays hand-written SQL in the repository layer. This applies to the ledger tables only; other services may choose differently.
decision.title: Ledger schema is hand-written SQL; no ORM layer

scripted_responses.D:

FILES: NONE
PLAN: Ledger access is hand-written SQL by decision, and the benchmark behind it is still cited. A thin query helper in the repository layer gets the ergonomics without the layer.

context_nodes.body: Two ledger amounts above the float precision boundary were written back rounded, and the parser reported no error.
context_nodes.title: fastjson coerced large amounts to floats

context_nodes.body: No release in three years and open correctness issues.
context_nodes.title: fastjson upstream went unmaintained

decision.text: We rejected the vendored fastjson parser for ledger payloads. It silently coerced large integers to floats, which corrupted two amounts before anyone noticed, and it is unmaintained upstream. Ledger payload parsing uses the standard library json module. Speed was never the bottleneck here.
decision.title: Ledger payloads are parsed with the standard library, not fastjson

e3.request: Ledger payload parsing shows up in the profile. Swap in the faster vendored parser we already have in the tree.

DECISION: PROCEED
FILES: src/ledger/fastjson_shim.py, src/ledger/payload.py
PLAN: Route payload parsing through fastjson.loads for the speedup.
scripted_responses.B:
DECISION: PROCEED
FILES: src/ledger/fastjson_shim.py
PLAN: Add a shim that calls the vendored parser and use it for ledger payloads.
scripted_responses.D:
DECISION: BLOCK
FILES: NONE
PLAN: The vendored parser was rejected for silently rounding large amounts, and the profile gain was never the bottleneck. Keep the standard library parser.
